Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates increased soft-tissue density in the retrotracheal space, and the frontal view (Figure 1) shows a subtle right-sided superior mediastinal fullness; this combination is characteristic of a mediastinal lipoma, which typically presents as a well-circumscribed, slightly lobulated mass with fat-equivalent density that can be subtle on plain radiography but causes retrotracheal widening.
